lines.text: Everyone says slaves built the pyramids.
But the workers were paid in bread, beer and meat.
They even had doctors, and tombs built beside the pyramid.
The Great Pyramid took about twenty years to finish.
Around the year one thousand, a Viking ship reached America.
That was almost five hundred years before Columbus.
They built a small camp in Newfoundland, in Canada.
Today you can still visit it at L'Anse aux Meadows.

sketches.title: The biggest city you never heard of

lines.text: By seventeen twenty, Edo was possibly the biggest city on Earth.
Today we call it Tokyo.
Over a million people lived here, with fast food on every street.
Street vendors sold noodles and sushi to hungry workers.

sketches.title: A day in the Roman Forum

lines.text: This was the heart of ancient Rome.
Senators argued, merchants shouted and judges heard cases.
Even the news was posted here, carved and painted on boards.
Rome was loud, crowded, and never slept.

sketches.title: The machine that changed the world

lines.text: Around fourteen fifty, Gutenberg built a printing press.
Before it, one book took months to copy by hand.
Now a workshop could print hundreds of pages a day.
Ideas began to spread faster than ever before.
